name: CD4049UB
full_name: Hex Inverting Buffer / Level Converter (CMOS, Unbuffered)
description: Six inverting buffers with high sink current (drives two TTL loads). Its input high level may exceed VDD, so it converts higher-voltage logic down to a lower supply on a single rail. Unbuffered (one inverting stage per gate), so biased mid-rail it also works as a linear amplifier, the basis of CMOS distortion circuits. The CD4050B is the non-inverting counterpart and shares this datasheet.

extra.variant: UB = unbuffered (single stage), usable as a linear amp
extra.drive: high sink current, drives 2 TTL loads
extra.level conversion: input high level may exceed VDD, single supply

typical_application: Hex inversion, high-to-low logic level conversion on a single supply, and CMOS current driving. The UB variant biased mid-rail is the classic CMOS distortion / oscillator gain stage.
gotchas: supply is pin 1 and ground is pin 8; pin 16 is NOT connected. Wiring VDD to pin 16 out of 16-pin DIP habit leaves the chip dead
pins 13 and 16 are NC on this package, unlike most 16-pin logic
the input high level is allowed to exceed VDD (that is the level-conversion feature) -- unusual for CMOS, where inputs normally must stay inside the rails
UB (unbuffered) and B (buffered) variants behave differently; the linear-amp and distortion tricks need the UB
inverting; the CD4050B is the pin-similar non-inverting version
notes: Pins and specs checked against TI SCHS046L (Aug 1998, rev Feb 2026). TI labels the gates A-F (inputs) and G-L (outputs); house names use the 1A/1Y convention with the vendor labels kept in datasheet_name.
